issues.title: Simplex invariance at simultaneous zero rates

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We collect in $\theta \coloneqq (\hat d_D, \hat d_T, \hat r_R, \hat f_0)$ the non-negative constants

issues.failure_explanation: The old assumptions make hat r_R and hat d_T merely nonnegative. When both vanish, the displayed threshold hat r_R/(hat r_R+hat d_T) is undefined, so the proof's sign split does not cover that admissible parameter value. Direct substitution into the preceding boundary dynamics gives zero derivative, but the proof never supplies that case.
issues.overall_effect: For abstract ensembles containing the simultaneous zero-rate endpoint, invariance is not fully proved as written. Consequently, the use of invariance to identify the original and truncated dynamics, and the formal results relying on that identification, require the omitted branch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the proof of Lemma lem:domain_invariance, separate the case hat r_R + hat d_T = 0 before using the quotient. Nonnegativity then implies hat r_R = hat d_T = 0, and direct substitution into the boundary dynamics on s = 0 gives dot r = 0 for every r in [0,1]. Retain the existing sign split when the denominator is positive. This proves the same simplex-invariance statement for all admitted parameters, so thm:exist_Gamma, lem:extension, and cor:rep_grad_J remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof genuinely omits an admissible zero-denominator branch, so the defect is not merely transcriptional. However, the missing case is resolved by a short, routine direct substitution, without a new assumption, new lemma, weakened guarantee, or alteration of the dependent chain.

issues.title: Unbound state time in the domain-invariance lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The literal conclusion repeats the assertion about x(t) for every value of tau while never binding t, so it does not state that the trajectory belongs to the simplex at each quantified time. The appendix instead fixes an arbitrary tau and performs every boundary calculation at that same time, establishing x(tau) in the simplex.
issues.overall_effect: Only the lemma's printed time quantification is malformed; the appendix already supplies the intended invariant-set argument used later in the paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unbound t in the lemma's conclusion by the quantified variable tau, so that it states x_u^theta(tau) is in Delta for every tau in [0,T]. No proof change is needed.
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces this variable correction: tau is the quantified time, t is otherwise unbound, and the appendix carries out the argument at an arbitrary tau. Correcting the symbol repairs no mathematical inference or construction.

issues.title: Four-component parameter declared five-dimensional

failure_location.quote: Throughout the paper, the space $\Theta\subset \R^5$ is assumed to be compact.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the old parameter space is contained in five-dimensional Euclidean space. The old paper actually defines each parameter as the four-component tuple (hat d_D, hat d_T, hat r_R, f_0), explicitly says that n_0 is not uncertain, and later uses a four-factor product for Theta and its measure. The material difference is one nonexistent coordinate, making the printed ambient-space declaration incompatible with the parameter object actually used.
issues.overall_effect: The parameter-space typing is locally inconsistent, although the subsequent theory only needs compactness and does not materially depend on the numeral five.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the declaration Theta subset of R^5 by Theta subset of R^4.
issues.why_classification: The old source consistently defines theta as a four-component tuple, explicitly excludes n_0 from the uncertain parameters, and later uses a four-factor parameter product and measure. Thus the numeral 4 is uniquely forced, and no argument depends on the erroneous numeral 5.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Throughout the paper, the space $\Theta\subset \R^{m}$ is assumed to be compact.

issues.title: Missing minimizer index in the Gamma-limit

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if we denote with $u^\star_N$ a minimizer of $\J_N$ for every $N\geq1$

issues.failure_explanation: For each N the theorem declares u_N^star to be a minimizer of J_N. It never declares or quantifies a control u^star, so J_N(u^star) is not a well-defined conclusion under the theorem's notation. The proof's minimizer-sequence setup supports the indexed expression J_N(u_N^star), not the printed one.
issues.overall_effect: The minimum-value convergence clause of the main Gamma-convergence theorem is malformed; its separate limiting-point clause is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace J_N(u^star) in the minimum-value convergence clause by J_N(u_N^star), using the minimizer sequence already introduced in the theorem. No proof change is required.
issues.why_classification: The theorem defines only u_N^star, and its proof invokes the standard convergence of minimum values for that minimizer sequence. The missing index is a uniquely recoverable transcription error rather than a defective mathematical inference.

issues.title: Wrong domain for the extended objective
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition advertises Gateaux differentiability at arbitrary L^2 controls and uses arbitrary L^2 perturbations, but its printed signature defines J' only on U. Under that signature, J'(u) and J'(u+epsilon v) need not be defined. The preceding extension definition and the proposition's proof instead establish the result for J' on the whole L^2 space.
issues.overall_effect: The full-space differentiability proposition has an ill-typed input contract. The preceding definition already supplies the intended extension, and the later constrained directional formula only needs the valid feasible specialization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the proposition's signature to J': L^2([0,T],R) to R, matching the immediately preceding extension definition. The proposition and proof then apply to the stated arbitrary L^2 controls and perturbations without further modification.
issues.why_classification: The preceding definition and explanatory prose explicitly define J' on all of L^2, while the proposition's evaluations require that same domain. The corrected signature is uniquely forced by the old source and repairs only an ill-typed declaration, not the proof.

issues.title: Free time variable in the adjoint equation
issues.failure_explanation: Within the advertised backward ODE, sigma is the independent variable while tau has no quantifier or definition. Consequently, the displayed right-hand side does not determine a unique adjoint curve in sigma. Differentiating the integral representation later in the old proof gives the required term evaluated at sigma, showing exactly what the proposition should state.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's advertised adjoint characterization is undefined as printed, and the corollary inherits that malformed adjoint equation in its gradient representation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the forcing term of eq:grad_back_ode, replace n_u^theta(tau) by n_u^theta(sigma). The corollary may continue to reference this corrected adjoint equation unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Sigma is the adjoint equation's independent variable, while tau is free there. Both the old integral representation and its differentiated formula evaluate the forcing at sigma, uniquely determining the correction. The same one-symbol repair also resolves the inherited corollary without changing any inference or guarantee.
